subject: Urgent: data-alert — coordination on notification path & evidence transfer
messages:
From: Max Turner <max.turner@finexcorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finexcorp.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Potential exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Hi Camila / Marissa,

Quick heads up — our security team detected what looks like an accidentally public S3 snapshot containing tokenized request logs that reference calls to Redwood’s hosted inference endpoints. We’re still triaging but wanted to loop you in immediately.

What we can share now:
- Short summary: S3 bucket "finex-prod-logs-archive" had a misapplied IAM policy for ~2 hours (approx 03:40–05:35 UTC).
- Affected artifacts: request logs with hashed customer identifiers and partial request metadata.
- We will provide a SIEM export and a snapshot manifest shortly (attaching pointers).

As this looks like it may trigger DPA notification obligations, can you confirm:
1) Redwood’s expected timeline for formal notification to customers under your DPA / breach clauses?
2) Contact for evidence ingestion and chain-of-custody (where we should upload the snapshot to you)?

We’d like to coordinate a single channel for evidence to avoid duplication.

Thanks,
Max Turner
Head of Security — FinexCorp

Attachment: s3_snapshot_manifest.txt (text, 4KB)
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Max Turner <max.turner@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Max — thanks for the alert and for the manifest.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood must comply with DPA notification obligations; our internal policy triggers an incident review and notification decision within the DPA window (we treat "notify without undue delay and no later than 72 hours" as the baseline but the final cadence depends on scope and customer impact).
- For evidence transfer: please upload a read-only snapshot to the secure evidence bucket we provision for incidents (I’ll send the link). We will provide a signed receipt and chain-of-custody confirmation.

A few asks to speed this up:
- Can you include the SIEM export (syslog + alert timeline) and a short list of unique customer IDs or tenant hashes that appear in the logs? We don’t need raw PII — hashed or tokenized IDs are fine for scope mapping.
- Confirm whether any subprocessors (e.g., backup/replication vendors) were involved in the snapshot lifecycle — name, contact, jurisdiction, and whether the copy left FinexCorp control.
- Indicate whether this snapshot contains full request payloads or metadata only.

Internal folks on this thread: Marissa, please own customer-facing comms once we have scope. Ben, please prepare to ingest SIEM and coordinate with Ops for chain-of-custody and a forensic snapshot. Laura (cc) — please advise on DPA clause interpretation below.

I’ll stand by for the upload link and will open an internal incident (JIRA-INC-78912).

— Camila
Director, Partnerships & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Camila / team — quick legal note and recommended next steps.

Legal position / DPA reference:
- Our standard DPA (Section 6.3 / Incident Notification) requires us to "notify without undue delay and, where required by applicable law, within 72 hours of becoming aware" of a personal data breach affecting customers. We should treat Finex’s report as "notification of an incident" and begin working to define impacted data subjects and customers.

Recommended approach:
1) Confirm scope within 24 hours (what tenants/hashes affected). If scope is limited to non-identifiable hashed IDs and metadata only, we may be able to push a mitigation-first notice to impacted accounts with a concise summary.
2) If raw request payloads or clear identifiers are present, we should prepare a formal DPA notification and coordinate joint customer comms where feasible.
3) Maintain chain-of-custody: require Finex to upload evidence to the secure upload location and to provide MD5/SHA256 checksums; Redwood will validate and issue a signed receipt.
4) Subprocessor involvement: if CloudSync (or other backup vendors) handled the snapshot, request their role, location (country), and whether they had temporary access. If a subprocessor contributed to the exposure, we must document that for DPA disclosures.

Operational asks:
- Ben: coordinate with Ops to ingest siem_export_20270528.tar.gz and validate timestamps.
- Camila / Marissa: prepare a short holding statement for customers that summarizes next steps and expected timeline (we typically communicate within 72h if the incident meets DPA thresholds).

I’ll loop in Compliance if we determine cross-border transfer / regulatory reporting is triggered.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@cloudsync.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Max Turner <max.turner@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure detected — immediate coordination requested

Hi all — Olivia from CloudSync (backup/subprocessor) here. We performed an emergency snapshot for FinexCorp during the window noted and our logs show the same S3 object was created from our replication job. A few clarifications:

- The object lifecycle: created 03:41 UTC, replicated to our archival node at 04:05 UTC; we did not advertise the object publicly — the misconfiguration originated in FinexCorp’s bucket policy.
- We have prepared the SIEM export and an encrypted archive (siem_export_20270528.tar.gz). I’ve shared a secure drive pointer to Finex and an upload link for Redwood.
- Jurisdiction: CloudSync’s replication node handling the snapshot is in US-West (no cross-border transfer outside the US).

Requests from CloudSync:
1) Please confirm the upload location for chain-of-custody and whether Redwood requires a signed evidence receipt.
2) We’d like Redwood to confirm whether the snapshot contains any raw customer identifiers; CloudSync can redact on our side if requested but would need firm guidance.

We are happy to coordinate a short joint statement with FinexCorp and Redwood to ensure customers see aligned facts.

— Olivia Grant
VP, Security Operations — CloudSync Inc.

Attachment: siem_export_20270528.tar.gz (encrypted tar, 48MB)
